description: Zeck provider substitution map (Deployment & Runtime Architecture D1.0 sections 3 and 19). Zeck owns authority; providers implement operational ports. Every concern has an owning port, a reference provider and a documented replacement target. Failure behavior is explicit per dependency: the authoritative relational store fails closed; every non-authoritative dependency has an explicit degraded mode. D-08 (WORK-060 / AVA-003) adds typed steady-state redundancy: every durable concern (relational state, artifact bytes, queue transport, hosting) declares exactly one alternate provider with a governed-procedure failover profile — automatic failover is unrepresentable, and a redundancy claim carries drill-measured evidence at exact revisions (deploy:drill provider-redundancy). Free-tier doctrine applies: disposable free-tier resources are never operationally critical.

alternate.substitutionTarget: any managed PostgreSQL provider hosting the HA standby replica (the WORK-057 topology is provider-agnostic: connection URLs only)

failover.procedure: deploy:drill authority-failover (the WORK-057 governed failover: split-brain guard, pg_promote, post-conditions, control-plane repoint)
failover.measurement: measured failover RTO/RPO by drill at the exact revision against the real topology; recovery RESTORES authority, it never reconstructs it

degradation.effect: Control-plane admission and every authority-bearing operation refuse. No datastore is silently promoted; no authority data exists outside PostgreSQL.

alternate.substitutionTarget: any S3-compatible object store (the D-07 artifact-exit substitution engine: endpoint+credentials only, digest-verified byte migration)

failover.procedure: deploy:drill artifact-exit (byte migration + verification through recoverArtifactBytes over two ObjectStorePort endpoints)
failover.measurement: measured artifact-exit RTO/RPO by drill at the exact revision; artifact metadata/provenance stay authoritative in PostgreSQL

degradation.effect: Operations requiring artifact bytes fail explicitly. Artifact metadata and provenance in PostgreSQL remain authoritative; no artifact bytes pass through PostgreSQL as a fallback.

alternate.substitutionTarget: any managed queue/broker implementing the QueueTransportPort contract

failover.procedure: deploy:drill queue-recovery (transport substitution + replay convergence through the EXISTING dispatch/execution idempotency — never provider dedup)
failover.measurement: measured queue-recovery RTO/RPO by drill at the exact revision; a queued message is never mistaken for execution success

degradation.effect: Execution admission continues through PostgreSQL authority; dispatch is deferred and backlogged. A queued message is never mistaken for execution success; queue state is never an authority claim.
Waiting orchestrations pause; execution status, budget state, policy state and ledger state remain authoritative in PostgreSQL and resume on recovery.
Locks, rate limits and cache entries fall back to conservative local behavior. Redis holds no authority data, so its outage cannot corrupt or redefine durable application authority.

alternate.substitutionTarget: any host running the repository-defined API entry (the D-07 proof: the server is provider-neutral by construction — configuration-only exit, no domain semantics change)

failover.procedure: operator re-points delivery at the alternate host running the same repository entry; readiness verified with deploy:smoke / deploy:release gate run health at the exact revision
failover.measurement: the health/readiness gate over the alternate host (control-plane availability facts, fail-closed semantics preserved); live provider execution is drill-measured where credentials exist

providers.commercialUse: Hobby-tier usage is permitted for personal/non-commercial development and preview only. Commercial production requires a commercially permitted plan; the API remains independently runnable so hosting can move without domain change.

degradation.effect: The experience layer is unreachable; control-plane and execution-plane authority are unaffected.

providers.substitutionTarget: any runner daemon implementing the documented container-runner REST protocol (first-party fleet runner or a governed customer runner)

degradation.effect: Container sandbox dispatch fails closed (runtime-unavailable); the execution stays durably recoverable in PostgreSQL and re-dispatches on recovery. No unisolated or ambient-host execution is ever a fallback; the execution authority is untouched.

providers.substitutionTarget: any OpenTelemetry-compatible collector (self-hosted or managed); the OTLP/HTTP-JSON protocol is a transport standard, not a vendor control plane

degradation.effect: Telemetry export is unconfigured or unreachable; the sink degrades to bounded structured local logs with drop counters. Observability never blocks the control or execution planes and never becomes an authority.
